nfrs.title: Sponsor List Scalability
nfrs.description: The system shall maintain sub-2-second response times for paginated sponsor lists even with 500 active sponsors and 100,000 unique monthly anonymous users viewing the page.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Load testing with a simulated dataset of 500 sponsors and 100,000 unique monthly user profiles (simulated over a day) viewing the sponsor list, ensuring 95% of requests complete within 2 seconds.
nfrs.rationale: US01 (List sponsors) needs to be viewable by many users without performance degradation, especially as the number of sponsors grows, ensuring a consistent user experience.

nfrs.title: Sponsor List Cross-Browser Compatibility
nfrs.description: The sponsor list, including sorting, filtering, and pagination, shall render correctly and be fully functional on the latest stable versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge, as well as mobile equivalents.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Manual and automated UI testing across specified browsers and mobile devices (iOS Safari, Android Chrome) confirms no layout issues, broken functionality, or unresponsive elements for US01.
nfrs.rationale: US01 (List sponsors) is for anonymous users, implying broad accessibility. Incompatible display on common browsers would prevent users from effectively viewing and interacting with the list.

nfrs.title: Cancellation Terms Acceptance Reliability
nfrs.description: The acceptance status of cancellation terms (checkbox state) shall be accurately recorded and permanently associated with the trainee's account for all successful submissions.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: For 100% of successful trainee registrations, verify through database inspection that the 'cancellation_terms_accepted' flag is set to true and remains immutable after acceptance.
nfrs.rationale: For US09 (Cancellation terms), accountability relies on the certainty that the trainee's acceptance is reliably recorded and cannot be lost or altered, which is critical for legal and operational reasons.

nfrs.title: Cancellation Terms Data Integrity
nfrs.description: The system shall prevent unauthorized modification or deletion of a trainee's acceptance of cancellation terms once recorded.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Attempt to modify or delete the acceptance status of a trainee's cancellation terms directly via API calls or database manipulation (excluding administrative deletion for support cases). Verify all attempts are blocked or logged as unauthorized.
nfrs.rationale: US09 (Cancellation terms) relies on accountability. Ensuring data integrity prevents malicious or accidental tampering with acceptance records, which is crucial for legal defensibility.

nfrs.title: Event Scheduling Reliability
nfrs.description: When a trainee adds an event to their schedule, the system shall successfully persist the event to the trainee's schedule and reflect it accurately within 0.5 seconds for 100% of valid requests.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Conduct functional tests where 100 trainee users simultaneously add an event to their schedule. Verify that all events are correctly added and immediately visible in "my schedule" without data loss or conflicts.
nfrs.rationale: For US11 (Add event to schedule), trainees need confidence that their schedule changes are saved correctly and immediately, preventing confusion or double-bookings.

nfrs.title: Event Scheduling Availability
nfrs.description: The "Add to My Schedule" feature shall have an uptime of 99.9% during the event registration and event period.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Monitor the availability and functionality of the "Add to My Schedule" feature using automated uptime monitoring tools over a 30-day period.
nfrs.rationale: US11 (Add event to schedule) relies on the feature being consistently available when trainees wish to manage their schedule, preventing missed opportunities or frustration.

nfrs.title: Venue Details Page Performance
nfrs.description: The venue details page, including images and embedded maps, shall fully load and be interactive within 3 seconds for 90% of anonymous users under normal load.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Utilize browser developer tools and performance testing (e.g., Lighthouse) to measure the Time to Interactive (TTI) for the venue details page for 90% of requests, ensuring it is under 3 seconds.
nfrs.rationale: For US25 (Venue description), anonymous users expect a fast loading experience. Slow pages, especially with rich media, can deter engagement and make it difficult to get a sense of the location.

nfrs.title: Venue Details Content Accessibility
nfrs.description: The venue details content (text, images, map if applicable) shall meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA guidelines to ensure accessibility for users with disabilities.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Conduct an accessibility audit using automated tools (e.g., axe-core) and manual review against WCAG 2.1 Level AA guidelines for US25. All detected violations must be remediated.
nfrs.rationale: US25 (Venue description) aims to provide location information to all users. Meeting accessibility standards ensures that users with visual or other impairments can also "get a sense of the location."

nfrs.title: Payment Information Security (PCI DSS)
nfrs.description: The system shall process, store (if applicable, in encrypted form), and transmit payment card information in a manner compliant with PCI DSS v3.2.1 requirements, including encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256).
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Conduct a PCI DSS compliance audit performed by a certified QSA. All identified vulnerabilities and non-conformities related to US30 payment processing must be addressed and verified.
nfrs.rationale: US30 (Process payment) involves sensitive financial data. PCI DSS compliance is non-negotiable for protecting user payment information and avoiding legal and financial repercussions.

nfrs.title: Payment Transaction Reliability
nfrs.description: The payment processing system shall ensure that 100% of valid payment attempts are either successfully processed with a confirmed charge or clearly fail with an appropriate error, preventing partial charges or ambiguous states.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Perform extensive functional and negative testing, including network interruptions, duplicate submissions, and invalid card data. Verify that for every transaction attempt, the system reaches a definitive success or failure state, and the user receives correct feedback, with no phantom charges.
nfrs.rationale: For US30 (Process payment), reliability is paramount. Ambiguous transaction states lead to user distrust, support overhead, and potential financial discrepancies.

nfrs.title: Payment Processing Response Time
nfrs.description: The system shall complete the payment authorization and confirmation process, including sending a transaction confirmation, within 5 seconds for 98% of successful transactions.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Monitor payment gateway response times and internal processing logs. 98% of transactions initiated via US30 must show a completion time (from submission to confirmation) of under 5 seconds.
nfrs.rationale: US30 (Process payment) is a critical user action. Slow payment processing can lead to user abandonment, frustration, and a perception of unreliability.

nfrs.title: Payment Error Messaging Usability
nfrs.description: For any failed payment transaction, the system shall display a specific, user-understandable error message that clearly indicates the reason for failure (e.g., "Card declined," "Insufficient funds," "Invalid card number").
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Test payment attempts with various invalid scenarios (e.g., expired card, incorrect CVC, declined by bank). For each scenario, verify that the displayed error message is specific, actionable, and user-friendly, as per US30's acceptance criteria.
nfrs.rationale: US30 (Process payment) explicitly requires appropriate error messages for failed transactions. Clear feedback helps users rectify issues and proceed, improving the overall payment experience.

nfrs.title: Sponsor Link Access Control
nfrs.description: Only authenticated users with the 'sponsor' role shall be able to create, modify, or delete links to their sponsorship page and associate attendees.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Attempt to perform sponsor linking actions (create, modify, delete) while logged in as an 'anonymoususer', 'authenticateduser', 'trainee', or another non-'sponsor' role. Verify all such attempts are denied with an "Access Denied" error.
nfrs.rationale: US31 (Assign sponsors) involves displaying potentially sensitive attendance data. Strong access control ensures that only authorized sponsors can manage this information, preventing data misuse or misrepresentation.

nfrs.title: Sponsor Link Data Reliability
nfrs.description: Links created by sponsors and their associated attendance data shall persist accurately and be accessible from the sponsorship page without degradation for the entire event duration (including post-event viewing period of 6 months).
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: After a sponsor creates links and associates attendees, verify the data immediately and at 30-day intervals for 6 months post-event. Confirm 100% accuracy and availability of all linked information.
nfrs.rationale: US31 (Assign sponsors) relies on the persistence and accuracy of linked data to "show off our level of attendance." Data loss or corruption would undermine the sponsor's goal.

nfrs.title: Tagging System Maintainability
nfrs.description: The tagging system for blog posts shall be implemented using a standard, well-documented API or framework component, allowing for easy updates and extensions by a Drupal developer.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Conduct a code review to confirm adherence to Drupal coding standards and use of core/contributed modules for tagging. A new tag vocabulary or term should be addable by a developer in under 15 minutes.
nfrs.rationale: US34 (Tag posts) is an administrative function. Good maintainability ensures that administrators can continue to effectively manage tags and integrate with external platforms like Drupal Planet without significant development overhead.

nfrs.title: Tag Publishing Reliability
nfrs.description: Once an administrator tags a blog post, the system shall ensure that the tag is correctly associated with the post and reflected in the relevant RSS feed or API endpoint for Drupal Planet within 1 minute of publication.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Publish 10 blog posts with tags relevant for Drupal Planet. Within 1 minute of publication, verify via direct inspection of the generated RSS feed or API response that all tags are correctly present.
nfrs.rationale: US34 (Tag posts) directly aims for posts to be listed on Drupal Planet. Reliable and timely tag application is essential for this outcome.

nfrs.title: User Event List Performance
nfrs.description: An attendee's list of signed-up summits shall load and display within 1.5 seconds for 95% of requests, even when the attendee is signed up for 20+ events.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Simulate a user logged in with 20+ assigned events. Conduct performance testing, ensuring 95% of requests to view "my summits" complete within 1.5 seconds under anticipated peak load.
nfrs.rationale: US40 (View events) is crucial for attendees to manage their schedule. A slow loading list would hinder their ability to confirm attendance and prevent double-booking.

nfrs.title: User Event List Data Accuracy
nfrs.description: The system shall display 100% accurate and up-to-date information regarding an attendee's signed-up summits, reflecting all confirmed registrations and cancellations without delay.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Conduct tests where attendees register for and cancel events. Immediately after each action, verify that their "my summits" list correctly reflects the changes. Ensure no outdated or incorrect entries are shown.
nfrs.rationale: US40 (View events) is for confirming attendance and preventing double-booking. Inaccurate data would directly defeat the purpose of the story, leading to confusion and scheduling errors.

nfrs.title: Job Listing Creation Security
nfrs.description: Only authenticated users with the 'sponsor' role shall be authorized to post new job listings.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Attempt to access the "Post Job" functionality and submit a job listing while logged in as an 'anonymoususer', 'authenticateduser', 'trainee', or another non-'sponsor' role. Verify all such attempts are denied.
nfrs.rationale: US52 (Post job listing) allows sponsors to advertise. Unauthorized posting could lead to spam or inappropriate content, harming the platform's reputation and sponsor value.

nfrs.title: Job Listing Data Persistence
nfrs.description: All submitted job listings shall be reliably stored and remain publicly visible (unless marked otherwise by the sponsor) for their specified duration, without accidental loss or corruption.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: After a sponsor posts a job, verify its presence immediately, and then periodically (e.g., daily) for the listing's full duration. Simulate database backups and restores, ensuring job listings remain intact.
nfrs.rationale: For US52 (Post job listing), sponsors expect their advertisements to remain visible. Data loss or corruption would undermine their ability to hire and their value proposition.

nfrs.title: Session Acceptance Authorization
nfrs.description: Only authenticated users with the 'administrator' role shall be able to mark a session as accepted.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Attempt to change a session's status to 'accepted' while logged in as an 'anonymoususer', 'authenticateduser', 'trainee', 'sponsor', or any non-'administrator' role. Verify all such attempts are denied.
nfrs.rationale: US58 (Accept session) is a critical administrative function. Unauthorized users accepting sessions could lead to an unmanageable or inappropriate event schedule.

nfrs.title: Session Status Change Reliability
nfrs.description: When an administrator marks a session as accepted, the system shall reliably update the session's status and persist this change, making it immediately reflected across all relevant views and APIs, 100% of the time.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: An administrator accepts 10 sessions. Verify via UI and API that all 10 sessions' statuses are correctly updated to 'accepted' and are immediately visible in schedule population features. Simulate system restart and confirm status persists.
nfrs.rationale: For US58 (Accept session), reliable and immediate status updates are essential for populating the schedule accurately and efficiently, preventing scheduling errors or discrepancies.

nfrs.title: Speaker Registration Data Security
nfrs.description: All speaker registration data, including personal information and session details, shall be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2+ and stored at rest using AES-256 encryption.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Conduct a security audit and penetration test. Verify that all data submitted via US62 registration forms is encrypted during transmission and stored in an encrypted format in the database.
nfrs.rationale: US62 (Speaker registration) collects personal and session data. Protecting this information from unauthorized access is critical for privacy and security, building trust with speakers.

nfrs.title: Speaker Registration Form Reliability
nfrs.description: The speaker registration form shall reliably submit and save all submitted data for 100% of valid submissions, even under peak load conditions of 50 concurrent registrations.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Conduct load testing simulating 50 concurrent speaker registrations. Verify that 100% of valid submissions are successfully processed, and all data is accurately stored without loss or corruption.
nfrs.rationale: US62 (Speaker registration) is a critical initial step for speakers. Unreliable submission would lead to lost sessions, frustration, and significant administrative overhead.

nfrs.title: Speaker Registration Form Usability Feedback
nfrs.description: Upon successful submission of the speaker registration form, the system shall provide clear, immediate visual confirmation (e.g., a "Thank You" page or success message) to the user.
nfrs.acceptance_criteria: Perform functional testing of US62 registration. Verify that after every successful submission, the user is redirected to a confirmation page or shown a clear, persistent success message, with no ambiguity.
nfrs.rationale: For US62 (Speaker registration), clear feedback reassures the anonymous user that their submission was received, preventing multiple submissions or confusion.

test_scenarios.title: Sponsor list performance with maximum sponsor data volume

test_scenarios.expected_outcome: Paginated sponsor lists render within 2 seconds for 95% of requests.

test_scenarios.title: Sponsor list rendering and functionality across desktop browsers
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Verify the sponsor list, including sorting, filtering, and pagination, renders and functions correctly on Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge (latest stable versions).
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: No layout issues, broken functionality, or unresponsive elements are observed on desktop browsers.

test_scenarios.title: Sponsor list rendering and functionality on mobile devices
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Verify the sponsor list displays and works correctly on mobile equivalents (iOS Safari, Android Chrome).
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The sponsor list content is responsive, readable, and fully functional on specified mobile browsers.

test_scenarios.title: Cancellation terms acceptance on successful trainee registration
test_scenarios.scenario_description: A trainee successfully registers, explicitly accepting the cancellation terms during the process.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The 'cancellation_terms_accepted' flag is accurately set to true and permanently associated with the trainee's account.

test_scenarios.title: Immutability of accepted cancellation terms after registration
test_scenarios.scenario_description: After a trainee successfully accepts cancellation terms, attempt to modify the recorded status through standard application flows.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The 'cancellation_terms_accepted' status remains true and cannot be altered by the user or regular system operations.

test_scenarios.title: Unauthorized API attempt to modify accepted cancellation terms
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Attempt to change a trainee's 'cancellation_terms_accepted' status directly via an unauthenticated or unauthorized API call.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The modification attempt is rejected, and the system logs the unauthorized access attempt.

test_scenarios.title: Direct database attempt to alter accepted cancellation terms
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Attempt to modify or delete the 'cancellation_terms_accepted' flag for a trainee directly in the database using non-privileged access.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The modification or deletion attempt is blocked by database constraints or permissions, or detected and logged as unauthorized.

test_scenarios.title: Event addition reliability under concurrent user activity
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Simulate 100 trainee users simultaneously adding events to their schedules.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: All events are successfully added to each trainee's schedule, immediately visible, and no data loss or conflicts occur.

test_scenarios.title: Single event addition persistence and display speed
test_scenarios.scenario_description: A single trainee adds an event to their schedule and immediately navigates to "my schedule".
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The event is successfully persisted and displayed in "my schedule" within 0.5 seconds.

test_scenarios.title: Availability of "Add to My Schedule" over extended period
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Continuously monitor the "Add to My Schedule" feature for functionality and accessibility over a 30-day period.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The "Add to My Schedule" feature maintains at least 99.9% uptime throughout the monitoring period.

test_scenarios.title: "Add to My Schedule" availability under peak load conditions
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Monitor the availability of the "Add to My Schedule" feature during simulated peak event registration traffic.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The feature remains available and functional, sustaining 99.9% uptime even during periods of high concurrency.

test_scenarios.title: Venue details page load time for anonymous users
test_scenarios.scenario_description: An anonymous user accesses the venue details page under typical system load conditions.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The venue details page is fully loaded and interactive within 3 seconds for 90% of requests.

test_scenarios.title: Venue page performance with heavy images and embedded map
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Test the venue details page when it contains a high number of images and a complex embedded map, under normal user load.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: Despite rich content, the page remains interactive within 3 seconds for 90% of anonymous user requests.

test_scenarios.title: Automated accessibility scan of venue details page
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Conduct an automated accessibility audit on the venue details page using tools like axe-core.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: No critical or severe WCAG 2.1 Level AA violations are detected by automated tools.

test_scenarios.title: Manual review of venue details content for WCAG compliance
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Perform a manual accessibility review of the venue details page, focusing on keyboard navigation, semantic structure, and logical focus order.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The venue details content meets all applicable WCAG 2.1 Level AA guidelines, with all interactive elements navigable and perceivable.

test_scenarios.title: Comprehensive PCI DSS compliance audit for payment system
test_scenarios.scenario_description: A certified QSA conducts a full PCI DSS v3.2.1 compliance audit of the payment processing system.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The system passes the PCI DSS audit, with no critical non-conformities identified regarding payment card handling.

test_scenarios.title: Verification of payment data encryption in transit and at rest
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Inspect network traffic during payment submission and analyze the storage of payment-related data in the database.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: Payment card information is encrypted using TLS 1.2+ during transit and AES-256 at rest (if stored).

test_scenarios.title: Definitive outcome for valid and invalid payment attempts
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Process a mix of valid payment attempts and deliberately invalid ones (e.g., incorrect CVC, expired card, insufficient funds).
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: Every valid attempt reaches a confirmed success, and every invalid attempt reaches a clear, documented failure state without ambiguity.

test_scenarios.title: Payment system behavior during network interruptions
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Simulate network connectivity issues or gateway timeouts during various stages of the payment transaction.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The system consistently resolves to either a successful charge or a definite failure with no partial charges or phantom transactions.

test_scenarios.title: Payment completion time under typical transaction volume
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Process a batch of successful payment transactions under average system load and monitor completion times.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: 98% of successful payment transactions, from submission to confirmation, complete within 5 seconds.

test_scenarios.title: Payment completion time under high concurrent transactions
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Simulate a peak period of high concurrent payment submissions by multiple users.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: Even under peak load, 98% of successful transactions achieve completion within 5 seconds.

test_scenarios.title: User-friendly error messages for standard payment failures
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Initiate payment attempts using scenarios such as an expired card, incorrect CVC, and intentionally insufficient funds.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The system displays clear, specific, and actionable error messages (e.g., "Card expired," "CVC incorrect") for each failure type.

test_scenarios.title: Specific error messages for less common payment failures
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Initiate payment attempts simulating less common issues, such as card issuer specific declines or general processing errors.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The system provides informative error messages that help the user understand the issue, even if more generic (e.g., "Transaction declined by bank").

test_scenarios.title: Anonymous user attempts sponsor link creation/modification
test_scenarios.scenario_description: An unauthenticated (anonymous) user attempts to access or perform any sponsor linking actions (create, modify, delete).
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: All attempts are denied with an "Access Denied" error or equivalent, and no unauthorized action is performed.

test_scenarios.title: Non-sponsor authenticated user attempts sponsor link actions
test_scenarios.scenario_description: An authenticated user with 'trainee' or general 'authenticateduser' role attempts to create, modify, or delete sponsor links.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: All attempts are denied with an "Access Denied" error, preventing any unauthorized sponsor linking actions.

test_scenarios.title: Immediate persistence of newly created sponsor links and data
test_scenarios.scenario_description: A sponsor creates new links and associates attendees with those links.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: All created links and associated attendance data are immediately and accurately reflected on the sponsorship page.

test_scenarios.title: Sponsor link and attendance data accessibility post-event
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Verify the availability and accuracy of sponsor links and associated attendance data at 30-day intervals for 6 months after the event concludes.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: All sponsor link and attendance data remains 100% accurate and accessible for the entire post-event viewing period.

test_scenarios.title: Tagging system code adherence to Drupal standards
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Conduct a code review of the tagging system implementation by an experienced Drupal developer.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The tagging system utilizes standard Drupal APIs/components and adheres to Drupal coding best practices, requiring no custom, difficult-to-maintain code.

test_scenarios.title: Ease of adding new tag terms to existing vocabulary
test_scenarios.scenario_description: A Drupal developer attempts to add a new term to an existing tag vocabulary within the system.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The developer successfully adds the new tag term and verifies its functionality in under 15 minutes.

test_scenarios.title: Tag reflection for a single blog post after publication
test_scenarios.scenario_description: An administrator publishes a new blog post with relevant tags.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The tags are correctly associated with the post and appear in the relevant RSS feed or API endpoint for Drupal Planet within 1 minute.

test_scenarios.title: Tag reflection for multiple blog posts published concurrently
test_scenarios.scenario_description: An administrator publishes 10 blog posts with distinct tags in quick succession.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: All tags for all 10 posts are correctly associated and reflected in the Drupal Planet RSS feed or API within 1 minute of their respective publications.

test_scenarios.title: Event list load time for user with many registered events
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Simulate a user logged in with 20+ assigned events accessing their "my summits" page under anticipated peak load.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The user's event list loads and displays within 1.5 seconds for 95% of requests.

test_scenarios.title: Event list load time for typical number of registered events
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Simulate a user logged in with an average number of registered events (e.g., 5-10) accessing their "my summits" page under normal load.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The user's event list loads and displays well within 1.5 seconds for 95% of requests.

test_scenarios.title: Immediate reflection of new event registrations in user list
test_scenarios.scenario_description: An attendee successfully registers for a new event.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The newly registered event immediately appears correctly in the attendee's "my summits" list.

test_scenarios.title: Immediate reflection of event cancellations in user list
test_scenarios.scenario_description: An attendee successfully cancels their registration for an event.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The cancelled event is immediately removed or correctly marked as cancelled in the attendee's "my summits" list.

test_scenarios.title: Anonymous user attempts to post a new job listing

test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The anonymous user is denied access to the feature and cannot submit a job listing.

test_scenarios.title: Non-sponsor authenticated user attempts to post a job
test_scenarios.scenario_description: An authenticated user with a 'trainee' or general 'authenticateduser' role attempts to post a new job listing.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The non-'sponsor' authenticated user is denied access to the "Post Job" functionality and cannot submit a job listing.

test_scenarios.title: Immediate storage and public visibility of new job listings
test_scenarios.scenario_description: A sponsor successfully posts a new job listing, marked as publicly visible.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The job listing is immediately stored, correctly associated with the sponsor, and visible on the public job board.

test_scenarios.title: Job listing persistence over its specified duration
test_scenarios.scenario_description: Verify the presence and integrity of job listings periodically (e.g., daily) throughout their specified public duration.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: All job listings remain accurately stored and publicly visible (if applicable) for their entire active period without loss or corruption.

test_scenarios.title: Non-administrator user attempts to accept a session
test_scenarios.scenario_description: An authenticated user (e.g., trainee, sponsor, or general authenticated user) attempts to change a session's status to 'accepted'.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The system denies the attempt with an "Access Denied" error or equivalent, preventing unauthorized session status changes.

test_scenarios.title: Anonymous user attempts to accept a session
test_scenarios.scenario_description: An unauthenticated (anonymous) user attempts to change a session's status to 'accepted' (e.g., via a direct API call).
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The system denies the attempt, typically requiring authentication first, and prevents any unauthorized action.

test_scenarios.title: Single session acceptance and immediate status reflection
test_scenarios.scenario_description: An administrator marks a single session as 'accepted' through the administrative interface.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The session's status is reliably updated to 'accepted', immediately reflected in all relevant UI views and API endpoints.

test_scenarios.title: Multiple session acceptances and status persistence after restart
test_scenarios.scenario_description: An administrator accepts 10 sessions. Immediately after, simulate a system restart or database failover.

test_scenarios.title: Verification of speaker registration data encryption in transit
test_scenarios.scenario_description: A speaker submits their registration form. Network traffic is intercepted and analyzed during the submission.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: All speaker registration data is transmitted encrypted using TLS 1.2 or a stronger protocol.

test_scenarios.title: Verification of speaker registration data encryption at rest
test_scenarios.scenario_description: After a speaker successfully registers, attempt to access the stored registration data directly from the database.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: Speaker registration data, including personal and session details, is stored in the database using AES-256 encryption.

test_scenarios.title: Speaker registration reliability under 50 concurrent submissions

test_scenarios.title: Single speaker registration form submission reliability

test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The form data is successfully processed, and all information is accurately stored without issues.

test_scenarios.title: Clear visual confirmation after successful registration
test_scenarios.scenario_description: A user successfully completes and submits the speaker registration form.
test_scenarios.expected_outcome: The user is immediately redirected to a dedicated "Thank You" or confirmation page, clearly indicating successful submission.

test_scenarios.title: Immediate persistent success message after registration
